subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A particle is moving in a straight line so that after t seconds its distance s (in cm) from a fixed point on the line is s = f(t) = 8t + t³. Find (i) the velocity at time t = 2 sec, (ii) the initial velocity, and (iii) the acceleration at t = 2 sec.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what initial velocity means, and how many expressions you need before substituting.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate for velocity and acceleration
steps.margin_note: First mark. This is a rectilinear motion question with three asks, but only two expressions are needed. Write v and a once, then read all three answers off them.
steps.memory_tip: Three questions, two expressions: v = ds/dt and a = dv/dt cover every part.
lines: This is a rectilinear motion question. Velocity v = ds/dt and acceleration a = dv/dt.

recall.must_convey: That v = ds/dt = 8 + 3t² and a = dv/dt = 6t.
accept: differentiate s to get eight plus three t squared
differentiate again to get six t
velocity is the first derivative and acceleration is the second
s ni differentiate cheste eight plus three t squared vasthundi
v is d s by d t and a is d v by d t

steps.why: All three parts are values of the same two expressions at particular times, so writing v and a first turns the rest of the question into three substitutions.
common_mistakes: Writing v = 8t + 3t² by differentiating only the cube.
Differentiating once and treating 8 + 3t² as the acceleration.
Substituting t = 2 into s, which gives the distance 24 and not a velocity.

steps.label: Answer the three parts
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Initial means at the start, so t = 0. Distance is in centimetres here, so velocity is cm/sec and acceleration is cm/sec² — do not write metres.
steps.memory_tip: Initial means the clock reads zero: put t = 0, not t = 1.
lines: (ii) Initial velocity is v at t = 0:  v = 8 + 3(0)² = 8

lines.text: ∴ velocity at t = 2 sec = 20 cm/sec,  initial velocity = 8 cm/sec,  acceleration at t = 2 sec = 12 cm/sec²

recall.must_convey: That v(2) = 20, the initial velocity is 8, and a(2) = 12, in centimetre units.
accept: at two seconds the velocity is twenty centimetres per second
initial velocity means t equals zero so it is eight
the acceleration at two seconds is twelve
initial velocity ante t equals zero, eight vasthundi
twenty, eight and twelve are the three answers

steps.why: Initial velocity is the velocity at the instant the motion is timed from, which is t = 0. Putting t = 0 into 8 + 3t² leaves the constant 8, so the constant term of v is always the initial velocity.
common_mistakes: Reading initial velocity as the velocity at t = 1, which gives 11.
Answering only part (i) and leaving (ii) and (iii) out.
Writing m/sec when the distance is given in centimetres.

insider_note: Velocity is the first derivative and acceleration the second, so differentiate twice before substituting. Initial velocity means t = 0, which picks out the constant term.
